title: "Captions and figure numbers"

## About

This page documents ways to use Quarto to add captions to figures and to enable automatic numbering.

## Setup

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

## Figure captions

There are several ways to add captions to your Quarto figures depending on how the figures are generated.

### R code chunk

If you create a figure using an R code chunk, you can add a caption by using the `fig-caption` argument in the code chunk options. See @fig-add-caption-to-r-chunk.

::: {#fig-add-caption-to-r-chunk}

````{{r}}
#| label: fig-my-plot
#| fig-cap: "This is my plot. I hope that you like it."

x_random <- rnorm(n = 100)
random_df <- data.frame(x = x_random)

random_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Random Data") + 
  theme_minimal()
````

This code shows how to add parameters to an R code chunk. The parameters are preceded by `#|`. 
The parameter values are specified as key-value pairs.
The key is the label before the colon `:`, and the value is what follows the colon
We need to label figures using `#| label: fig-<name>`, where the figure name is specified as `fig-<name>`; here it is `my-plot`.
This makes sure that your Quarto document assigns a unique name to your figure.
We also need a `#| fig-cap:` parameter (cap is short for caption) to add a caption.
:::

The figure rendered by @fig-add-caption-to-r-chunk is as follows:

```{r}
#| label: fig-my-plot-rendered
#| fig-cap: "This is my plot. I hope that you like it."

x_random <- rnorm(n = 100)
random_df <- data.frame(x = x_random)

random_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Random Data") + 
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Titles can coexist with captions.

We can make figures with titles using `labs(title = "Histogram of Random Data")` or the `ggtitle()` function.
The same figure can have a caption added using `fig-cap: "This is a caption"` in the chunk options.
:::

### Images

If you include an image from the internet or a local file, it's easy to add a caption.

The syntax for adding an image is `![Caption goes 
here](url_or_path_to_file_goes_here)`.

So the following:

```markdown
![Nittany Lion Shrine from brand.psu.edu.](https://brand.psu.edu/images/backgrounds/warneke-shrine_v1_1.jpg)
```

yields

![Nittany Lion Shrine from brand.psu.edu.](https://brand.psu.edu/images/backgrounds/warneke-shrine_v1_1.jpg)

::: {.callout-important}
## Where did the figure number go?

Notice that the above image does not have a figure number, unlike the previous ones.
What gives?

The answer is that we need to give the figure its own unique #fig-\<name\> identifer.

:::

To give an included or embedded image a sequential figure number, we need to add something to the Quarto code that embeds the image.
You might have to scroll horizontally to see all of the code.

```markdown
![Nittany Lion Shrine from brand.psu.edu.](https://brand.psu.edu/images/backgrounds/warneke-shrine_v1_1.jpg){#fig-lion-shrine}
```

Now that our embedded figure has its own `#fig-name`, Quarto gives it a sequential figure number.
See @fig-lion-shrine) below.

![Nittany Lion Shrine from brand.psu.edu.](https://brand.psu.edu/images/backgrounds/warneke-shrine_v1_1.jpg){#fig-lion-shrine}

### Videos, code chunks, etc.

You can turn many bits of Quarto code into figures using a special syntax that wraps the code in pairs of triple colons `:::` as shown in @fig-video-chunk-code.

::: {#fig-video-chunk-code}

````markdown
::: {#fig-video}

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/plWh-hfM8I8?si=V1UFWZDl_Cmq5doB" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This is a video from YouTube.
:::
````

Quarto code to embed a video with a caption.
:::

The code in @fig-video-chunk-code code renders as follows:

::: {#fig-video}

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/plWh-hfM8I8?si=V1UFWZDl_Cmq5doB" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This is a video from YouTube.
:::
